content: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) is a professional organization composed of medical doctors in the United States who specialize in the fields of obstetrics and gynecology. Members of this organization are board-certified obstetrician-gynecologists and are referred to as Fellows. These individuals use the post-nominal letters FACOG to signify their status as Fellows of the College. To achieve the status of Fellow, candidates must successfully complete a rigorous two-part examination process that is conducted annually. The first part of this process is a written examination, which candidates are required to take during the first year they become eligible. Upon passing the written exam, candidates proceed to the second part, which is an oral examination. This oral exam is typically taken the year following the successful completion of the written portion. The oral examination is based on a comprehensive collection of clinical cases managed by the candidate over the course of a year, referred to as the case list. This process is known to be highly stressful for many physicians, with some even temporarily pausing their medical practices to dedicate sufficient time to preparation. The format and content of each section of the examination may vary from year to year, necessitating that candidates remain in close communication with ACOG and their peers for updated advice and guidance. In response to the challenges associated with this certification process, an entire industry has emerged to support candidates. This includes the provision of coaching services and review materials designed to help candidates prepare effectively for the examinations.
